- **Zero and positional notation** [`zero_place_value`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/zero_place_value.md) — K3, use correct, make easy, accept high. Merchants reckon with the nine figures and zero, but formal ledgers and sums are written in Roman numerals, thought harder to falsify. Local: abacus schools.
- **Hindu-Arabic numerals and written arithmetic** [`arabic_numerals`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/arabic_numerals.md) — K3, use correct, make easy, accept medium. Taught in six abacus schools to merchants' sons. The money-changers' guild forbade the new figures in account books in 1299; clerks and notaries keep Roman numerals. Local: Paolo dell'Abbaco's school by Santa Trinita; Arte del Cambio.
- **Abacus and counting board** [`abacus_counting_board`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/abacus_counting_board.md) — K3, use partial, make easy, accept low. In Tuscany 'abbaco' means pen reckoning with numerals; counters on a board survive in some offices and are northern habit. A bead frame is unknown. Elsewhere: France, England and Germany (reckoning counters); China (counting rods, early suanpan).
- **Common fractions and the rule of three** [`fractions_rule_of_three`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/fractions_rule_of_three.md) — K4, use correct, make easy, accept high. The daily bread of commerce: exchange, alloying, partnership shares are all solved by the rule of three. Local: abacus schools; Paolo dell'Abbaco.
- **Decimal fractions** [`decimal_fractions`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/decimal_fractions.md) — K0, use none, make easy, accept medium. Merchants use common fractions and mixed units (lire, soldi, denari); astronomers use sixtieths. Nobody in Europe writes tenths and hundredths positionally. Elsewhere: Islamic lands (al-Uqlidisi, al-Samaw'al); China, decimal fractions in rod numerals.
- **Negative numbers** [`negative_numbers`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/negative_numbers.md) — K1, use partial, make easy, accept medium. A negative answer is read as a debt, following Fibonacci, or thrown out as absurd. Ledgers keep what is owed and what is due apart. Elsewhere: India and China.
- **Square roots and irrational numbers** [`square_roots_irrationals`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/square_roots_irrationals.md) — K3, use partial, make easy, accept high. Abacus masters extract roots by hand and call the inexact ones deaf (radici sorde). Whether these are numbers at all is doubted. Local: Paolo dell'Abbaco.
- **Logarithms** [`logarithms`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/logarithms.md) — K0, use none, make medium, accept high. Tables must be computed by hand: months of work for a team of abacus masters. Needs decimal fractions first; astrologers gain most. Local: abacus masters.
- **Slide rule** [`slide_rule`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/slide_rule.md) — K0, use none, make medium, accept high. Needs a logarithm table first, then someone to engrave the scales on boxwood or brass; astrolabe makers are few. Local: goldsmiths and engravers.
- **Symbolic algebra** [`symbolic_algebra`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/symbolic_algebra.md) — K2, use partial, make easy, accept medium. Algebra is written out in words: cosa for the unknown, censo for its square. Vernacular treatises are a generation old; no signs for plus, minus or equals. Local: abacus masters; Maestro Dardi of Pisa's algebra (1344).
- **Solving quadratic and cubic equations** [`quadratic_cubic_equations`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/quadratic_cubic_equations.md) — K3, use partial, make medium, accept high. Abacus masters teach the six quadratic cases by rule. Dardi lists 198 cases with a few special cubics; other masters pass on false cubic rules. Local: abacus masters; Maestro Dardi of Pisa's algebra (1344).
- **Systems of linear equations (elimination and matrices)** [`linear_equations_matrices`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/linear_equations_matrices.md) — K2, use partial, make easy, accept medium. Problems with several unknowns are solved by single and double false position, case by case. An array of coefficients worked by elimination is unknown. Elsewhere: China, fangcheng array method.

- **Prime numbers and number theory** [`prime_numbers_number_theory`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/prime_numbers_number_theory.md) — K2, use partial, make easy, accept low. Euclid's books on numbers (Campanus' Latin) and Boethius are studied; perfect numbers interest theologians for their meaning, not their use. Elsewhere: Persia, al-Farisi on factorisation and amicable numbers.
- **Combinatorics (permutations, combinations, Pascal's triangle)** [`combinatorics_permutations`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/combinatorics_permutations.md) — K1, use none, make easy, accept medium. Players of zara know which three-dice totals come up most; a Latin poem, De vetula, counts the 216 throws. Llull's art combines letters on wheels. Local: dice players. Elsewhere: Provence, Levi ben Gerson's Hebrew proofs (1321); China, the arithmetic triangle (Zhu Shijie 1303).
- **Compound interest and exponential growth** [`compound_interest_exponential_growth`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/compound_interest_exponential_growth.md) — K4, use correct, make easy, accept medium. Bankers compound yearly (fare capo d'anno). Open interest is usury, so it hides in exchange rates and 'gifts'. The Bardi and Peruzzi have just failed. Local: Monte Comune (public debt consolidated in 1345, paying 5 per cent); money-changers of the Arte del Cambio; abacus schools.
- **Deductive geometry and proof (Euclid, Pythagoras)** [`geometry_proof`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/geometry_proof.md) — K3, use partial, make easy, accept high. Euclid exists in Campanus' Latin in costly manuscripts. Universities read the first books; craftsmen and abacus pupils learn recipes for areas and volumes without proof. Local: abacus schools; friars' schools.
- **Pi and the measurement of the circle** [`pi_circle_measurement`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/pi_circle_measurement.md) — K3, use correct, make easy, accept medium. Craftsmen use 22/7 and many take it for exact. Squaring the circle is still thought possible. Elsewhere: China, Zu Chongzhi's 355/113.
- **Trigonometry** [`trigonometry`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/trigonometry.md) — K2, use partial, make medium, accept medium. Sine tables come with the astronomical tables and serve astrologers only. Heights are measured with the shadow square of quadrant and astrolabe. Local: Paolo dell'Abbaco. Elsewhere: Avignon, Latin version of Levi ben Gerson's treatise on sines (1342); Oxford, Richard of Wallingford's Quadripartitum; Maragha tradition (al-Tusi).
- **Coordinate geometry and graphs of functions** [`coordinate_geometry`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/coordinate_geometry.md) — K1, use none, make easy, accept medium. Astronomers give star places by longitude and latitude; sea charts use compass lines, not a grid. Oxford masters speak of 'latitudes of forms' in words, without drawing them. Local: Pisan and Genoese sea charts. Elsewhere: Oxford, Merton calculators; Paris, the student Nicole Oresme (his graphs come c. 1350).
- **Non-Euclidean geometry** [`non_euclidean_geometry`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/non_euclidean_geometry.md) — K0, use none, make hard, accept low
- **Linear perspective and technical drawing** [`perspective_technical_drawing`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/perspective_technical_drawing.md) — K1, use partial, make easy, accept high. Giotto's followers paint convincing rooms by eye, with no vanishing-point rule; 'perspectiva' means optics. Buildings are made from parchment elevations and full-size templates. Local: Taddeo Gaddi; Andrea Orcagna; Ambrogio and Pietro Lorenzetti (Siena; both die in 1348); Opera del Duomo.
- **Surveying, levelling and triangulation** [`surveying_triangulation`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/surveying_triangulation.md) — K2, use partial, make medium, accept high. Land is measured with rods and cords, levels taken with a plumb-line frame; Fibonacci's Practica geometriae gives the rules. No scale maps of the territory exist. Local: the commune's sworn measurers; abacus masters (who teach land measuring). Elsewhere: Provence, Levi ben Gerson's cross-staff.
- **Solar calendar with leap years** [`solar_calendar_leap_years`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/solar_calendar_leap_years.md) — K4, use partial, make easy, accept medium. The spring equinox falls about nine days before 21 March. Florence starts the year on 25 March. Reform is the pope's business; he took advice in 1345. Elsewhere: Avignon, Jean de Murs and Firmin de Belleval's reform proposal for Clement VI (1345).
- **Decimal, coherent system of units (metric system)** [`metric_system_units`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/metric_system_units.md) — K0, use none, make medium, accept low. Every city has its own braccio, libbra and staio, and guards them as a sign of sovereignty. Merchants live with conversion handbooks such as Pegolotti's. Local: Pegolotti's Pratica della mercatura (compiled c. 1340).
